Impact: north-star leg A — every agent that trusts the advertised discovery card fails to reach the live MCP server (live-probed: card says sse at /api/mcp -> 404; real server is Streamable HTTP at /mcp -> serving)

# 265 — PR explainer (HIGH tier)

## Goal

Every agent that trusts DeFi Garden's own published MCP discovery card was
being misdirected to a 404. Item 228 shipped a real MCP server at `POST
/mcp` (Streamable HTTP, `tools`-only capability), but the three
`.well-known/` discovery cards `vercel.json:171` broadcasts a `Link` header
to on *every response the site serves* still said `url:
"https://www.defi.garden/api/mcp"`, `type: "sse"`, and claimed a `prompts`
capability the server has never implemented. This item makes the advertised
surface match the real one, and adds a test that keeps them matching.

## Intuition — why the mismatch existed, how it was found

The card has pointed at `/api/mcp` since item 223 first stubbed it — before
item 228's server existed at all, so the card wasn't wrong when it was
written, it was *aspirational*. 228 built the real server at `/mcp` instead
of the free-telemetry `/api/mcp` on purpose (mounting under `/api/*` would
have gotten MCP invocations classified `path_class = 'api'`, defeating
NORTH_STAR leg (A)'s two-term decomposition into API calls + MCP
invocations) — but nobody went back and updated the card that predates that
decision. 228's verifier caught it by hand, three rounds running: round 1
found the operator had written "no discovery document exists" into the spec
without opening the stubs; round 2 found the correction only named 2 of the
3 byte-identical cards; round 3 found the enumeration itself was still
under-inclusive — `validate_readiness.py` and `dns-aid-zone.txt` also
hardcode `/api/mcp`, invisible to a glob scoped to "cards" rather than "mcp"
paths generally. Filed as backlog 265 rather than fixed inline, because the
right fix is a genuine choice (correct the cards, or alias `/api/mcp`) that
228's scope didn't cover — and because at filing time the server wasn't
deployed yet, so the mismatch was latent, not live. The 2026-08-12 heartbeat
found the human had deployed it: the mismatch went from a paper defect to
live agents hitting a 404 today, which is what moved this item to the top
of the backlog.

## What changed and why, in reading order

1. **The three cards** (`.well-known/mcp.json`, `.well-known/mcp/server-card.json`,
   `.well-known/mcp/server-cards.json`) — corrected `url` to
   `https://www.defi.garden/mcp`, `type` to `streamable-http`, and dropped
   the `prompts` capability block, keeping only `tools: {list, call}`. Chose
   option (i) — correct the cards — over serving `/api/mcp` as an alias:
   smaller diff, no new route for `edge/agent-log.mjs` to maintain, and it's
   what the spec's own "Change" section calls the smaller of the two.
2. **`validate_readiness.py:62`, `dns-aid-zone.txt:14`, `SKILL.md:74`** —
   the three further deployed artifacts 228's round-3 verifier found also
   hardcoding `/api/mcp`. All three now say `/mcp`.
3. **`edge/MCP.md`** — appended a resolution paragraph directly after the
   existing "Not fixed in this item, on purpose" narrative (left untouched
   — it's the record of how the defect was found), stating what's now
   corrected and pointing at the new test.
4. **`test_mcp_discovery_cards.js`** (new) — the guard. Walks `.well-known/`
   for `mcp`-in-path files that parse as JSON with a `transports` key
   (never a hardcoded 3-file list), and checks every one against
   `edge/mcp-core.js`'s own `SERVER_CAPABILITIES` export and live
   `tools/list`/`tools/call` behaviour — set-equal, both directions — plus
   a pure-Node repo-wide walk proving no other file outside a documented,
   individually-justified historical/test allowlist still says `api/mcp`.
5. **`package.json`** — wired the new test into `test:serial`.

## Deviations from spec

- **Transport-type string** (`"streamable-http"`) is a stated constant, not
  derived from any JS export — the cards' own `$schema` URL 404s, so it
  can't be checked against a live registry spelling. Recorded, not
  blocking, per the spec's own allowance.
- **The `api/mcp`-residue allowlist ended up wider** than the five items the
  build prompt named: it also legitimately covers several
  `product-loop-kit/specs/*.md`/`signals/*.md` files (historical evidence,
  same role the repo already grants all of `product-loop-kit/**`),
  `edge/MCP.md`'s preserved historical narrative, and the new test file
  itself (which must name the string it hunts). Full accounting in
  `specs/265-notes.md`.
- `test_llms_rails.js` (an optional extra test) fails in this sandbox for
  an unrelated, pre-existing reason: no `node_modules/` installed at all.

## Quiz

1. The population of MCP discovery cards is derived by walking
   `.well-known/` and filtering to JSON files with a `transports` key,
   rather than hand-listing the three known filenames. What specific class
   of future bug would a hand-typed 3-file list fail to catch that the
   derived population does catch?
2. Describe the two mutations performed to prove `test_mcp_discovery_cards.js`
   is non-vacuous, and what each one's failure message named as wrong.
3. The build prompt's `api/mcp`-residue allowlist named five specific
   locations. The shipped test's allowlist is wider. What additional class
   of file did the repo-wide walk legitimately find, and what's the
   precedent for treating it as historical rather than fixing it?
4. Why does deriving the expected capability set from `edge/mcp-core.js`'s
   own `SERVER_CAPABILITIES` export (rather than hand-typing `["tools"]` as
   a separate literal in the test) matter more here than it might in a
   test that only checks today's three cards?
5. The `streamable-http` transport-type string could not be verified
   against the cards' own declared `$schema`. Why not, and what did the
   test do instead of blocking on it?
